findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django querysets is unsupported and exposes an unsafe path
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset < 0`). Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" is wrong. The cursor offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative ints). Any admin passing `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative offset will get a 500. The comment about 'data beyond normal pagination bounds' suggests the feature is meant to bypass pagination bounds, which is a risk in itself.

findings.title: Undocumented user-controlled query flag switches the audit-log endpoint onto an experimental paginator
findings.body: `optimized_pagination=true` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, gated only by `is_superuser or member.has_global_access`. That is a broad gate (every org owner/manager). This is unrelated to the PR title (spans buffer) and it exposes the unsafe negative-offset path on an audit-log API. Also `organization_context.member` can be None (e.g. for superusers not in the org), which would raise AttributeError. The `request.user.is_superuser or ...` evaluation order means non-superusers without a member would crash.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors to every paginator
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behavior for all BasePaginator subclasses used across Sentry. For `is_prev` cursors with a negative offset (user-controlled via the cursor string), the slice is now negative and raises an AssertionError (500) instead of being clamped. The justification comment is wrong. This is an unrelated, risky change to core pagination.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trim uses raw offset inconsistent with the slice actually used
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator, the condition `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses `offset`, while the slice was computed from `start_offset`. With a negative offset the lengths do not match, so the extra row is never trimmed and pages come out with the wrong size. The class also duplicates most of BasePaginator.get_result, and its `get_item_key` lacks datetime handling, so ordering by `-datetime` will fail with `math.floor(datetime)` TypeError.

findings.title: Redirect traversal depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment removed. Span trees deeper than 1000 will no longer resolve to the correct root set, silently producing split segments. This is not mentioned in the description.

findings.title: Eviction hard-codes 1000 while Python max_segment_spans is 1001; span_count may be stale
findings.body: The Lua script trims to 1000 spans with `zpopmin`, but the `max_segment_spans` config (1001) is still defined in `SpansBuffer`, and the Python-side span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, leaving it unused. Also, `span_count` is only the result of the last zunionstore. The payloads for the current span are zadded in Python before the script, so if neither union happens the zcard fallback is used, but if the first union ran and the second did not, the count reflects only the first union. That is fine, but the limit is not configurable and diverges from the config value.

findings.title: Switching from SET to ZSET without migration breaks in-flight data and dedups by payload only
findings.body: Keys with the same names (`span-buf:s:*`) change type from set to sorted set. During rollout, existing set keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors in `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zscan`, breaking the consumer. Also, `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is now required in `process_batch`, so any span lacking it raises KeyError and crashes the batch.

findings.title: No tests for eviction behavior or new paginator
findings.body: The PR adds span eviction at 1000 spans, a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, and negative offset handling, but the tests only add the new `end_timestamp_precise` field. No test covers the eviction ordering (oldest dropped), nor the paginator or audit log changes.
